Maya: Proposal: reduce SIEM raw export retention in S3 from 400d -> 90d to reduce PII exposure and cost. Need a defensible preserve/unlock runbook so IR/legal can access 1y+ snapshots when justified. Thoughts?
Priya: Strong preference for Object Lock for preserves. We should tag objects with x-case-id and promote to a locked copy on approval. Legal: COMPLIANCE mode if they insist, otherwise GOVERNANCE. Need clear ticketing integration.
Leo: KMS guidance: use envelope encryption with CMK; do not hand out long-lived decrypt keys. Create per-request KMS grants tied to ticket id + approver identity. All GrantCreate/Decrypt events are audited in CloudTrail.
Quinn: For partners, keep masked/aggregated partner-view for 365d; raw stays 90d. Nightly scrub job writes both buckets; partner bucket uses partner CMK + cross-account role.
Maya: Operational flow sketch: 1) user opens SEC ticket with case id and justification; 2) controller copies objects to forensics-archive, sets tag x-case-id, applies Object Lock (GOVERNANCE by default); 3) on approved unwrap, controller creates short-lived KMS grant tied to ticket, mints timeboxed presigned URL via SSO-proxy; 4) emit security-log audit entry.
Priya: Also require Privacy signoff for scrub rules and Finance signoff for storage + KMS HSM costs before finalizing retention numbers.
Leo: Test plan: staging expiry deny -> create object ttl=10s, wait 12s expect OPA deny/403; approval path -> copy to locked bucket, create grant, perform download, assert CloudTrail + security-log entry. Sample audit line (indexed string): ts=2026-03-20T12:01:05Z event=snapshot_unwrap case=CASE-2026-555 requester=leo approver=priya grant=g-7a6b5c object=forensics/CASE-2026-555-20260319.tar.gz ticket=SEC-5342
